reasoning: Scientific evidence confirms that octopuses have three hearts and blue blood. They possess two branchial hearts, which pump deoxygenated blood to the gills to absorb oxygen, and one systemic heart, which circulates the oxygenated blood to the rest of the body. Their blood is blue because it relies on a copper-based protein called hemocyanin to transport oxygen (unlike the iron-based hemoglobin in human blood). When hemocyanin binds with oxygen, it turns blue; when it is deoxygenated, the blood becomes colorless.
